CLINICAL TRANSLATION: The primary endpoint (HbA1c change at week 16) was never formally assessed for statistical significance — the trial was terminated early for commercial/business reasons (Pfizer returned worldwide rights for Exubera to Nektar in October 2007), not for safety or efficacy failure. The weight-based arm showed numerically larger glucose reductions across all biomarkers, suggesting dose-response relationship. Hypoglycemia was more frequent in the weight-based arm early (8.3/month vs 3.3/month at week 4) but equalized by week 16 (2.5 vs 2.4/month).

The primary endpoint was never formally evaluated (p-value = null, primary_endpoint_met = null). The trial was small (n=49) and was a dose-comparison study without a placebo arm, making it impossible to assess absolute efficacy vs. no treatment. The biology clearly moved in both arms, suggesting the mechanism was working.
